answer: Every dive to the vent field records the chimney temperatures, and the log holds a reading for each chimney the crew has visited. A terrace temperature copied from another expedition fails the log: at the beacon of the chimney the reading must match the dive's own instruments, and a copied number is off by degrees. Forging a log takes a submersible, three dives and 36,500 in vessel time, and the willow stamp on the logbook is countersigned by the dive master, so a chimney whose temperature was never measured is struck from the record.
